code_findings.finding: The scanner emits a false NOT_FOUND for every capability that lives inside a skipped or unexamined subtree. Proven directly: scanning a directory containing a .git/ subdirectory yields both 'excluded_subtree .git NOT_CHECKED' and 'version_control NOT_FOUND - not present anywhere in the authorized directory'. found[version_control] is only set in the file branch (after the d.IsDir() early return), so a .git directory can never set it. The same class applies to go.mod/package.json/requirements.txt under node_modules, vendor, dist, build, and to anything beyond MaxScanDepth=8 or MaxInventoryEntries=200 - a truncated walk still writes NOT_FOUND for every capability it never reached, and the truncation marker itself is dropped by add() once the cap is hit.
code_findings.recommendation: Track whether the walk was complete. If any subtree was skipped, capped or truncated, emit NOT_CHECKED with the reason instead of NOT_FOUND for capabilities not observed, and set the version_control capability from the .git directory as well as the .git file. Add fixture cases (a directory with .git/, a tree deeper than 8, a tree with >200 inventoried files) so the rule is asserted. Fix in W04-01 rework; it is squarely inside this card's write scope and its own governing rule (不能把未访问等同于没有).

code_findings.finding: The receipt's registry_continuation claim - 'this registration cannot shadow them' - is false. dispatch.py resolve_registry() prefers the v2.4 registry whenever the key exists there and the pointer is valid, so adding test.context at rev 8 captured auto resolution from the legacy entry and narrowed the accepted selectors: test.context --task-id W06 --check-id W06-G02, W12/C13, W17/C02 and case ids C01, C02, C13 all now return NOT_IMPLEMENTED (exit 3). Before rev 8 they resolved to execution/commands.json, whose test.context entry lists task_id W04/W06/W12/W17 and case_id C03/C04/A01/C01/C13/C02. The executor verified only --case-id A01, which is present in both lists and therefore cannot detect this. Explicit --spec v2.0 still reaches them (W17 C02 PASS 22 in my run), so the loss is a routing regression rather than permanent.

code_findings.area: tests/context/check/main.go assertion coverage of the binding lifecycle
code_findings.finding: Per-principal isolation of authorized_workspace_ref is entirely unasserted outside bootstrap: ListWorkspaceBindings' principal filter (V14, V14b), WorkspaceBindingFor's principal check (V21) and RevokeWorkspaceBinding's principal check (V22) can each be deleted or inverted with the suite still reporting PASS 123. A live probe through the public API confirmed the consequence: a second principal holding the global OWNER role reads another principal's binding including its real path, lists all four of that principal's bindings, and calls BootstrapProject against a foreign authorized_workspace_ref - which is ACCEPTED, returns the foreign project identity and its inventory, and inserts an auth_grant row giving the caller that project. Mitigation I verified: internal/host/bootstrap.go guarantees exactly one OWNER per local user, so the exploit needs a second OWNER provisioned through the trusted local admin path, and it does not cross OS users. It is nevertheless a real authorization escalation inside one machine and it contradicts the doc comment on ListWorkspaceBindings ('never another project's or another user's directories'), which the OWNER branch defeats.
code_findings.recommendation: Provision a second OWNER-capable principal in the check and assert that its list is empty of the first principal's refs, that WorkspaceBindingFor/Revoke refuse it, and that BootstrapProject against a foreign ref is refused or documented as an intentional owner-wide grant. Either way the comment and the code must agree. Owner: W04-01 rework.

code_findings.area: card requirement 2 - import failures recorded per file
code_findings.finding: The durable per-file failure record is unasserted end to end. Deleting the out.Failures append for an unparseable .json (V10b) and deleting the failuresList() persistence into the BootstrapStage row (V10c) both leave PASS 123, because INV-PARTIAL-PARSE-HAS-A-RECORD and INV-FAILURE-USES-RELATIVE-PATH read only the inventory entry's Notes string. The code path exists and works; nothing proves it stays.
code_findings.recommendation: Assert the stage record's file_failures array (path, reason, content_disclosed) from the durable row, not just the Notes substring. Owner: W04-01 rework.

code_findings.finding: 'Re-imports of identical content dedupe there' is false for this flow. upload() always INSERTs a fresh storage_key with no lookup by content_hash, and collectInventory stamps observed_at with Now(), so the payload bytes differ on every bootstrap. My probe ran six repeat bootstraps over an unchanged directory: domain_versions for kind=BootstrapStage grew 18 -> 24 and a new Artifact plus a new uploaded_content blob appear each time - the behaviour INV-REPEAT-ADDS-ONE-OBSERVATION deliberately asserts.
code_findings.recommendation: Correct the reuse note, and decide whether an unchanged re-scan should mint a new sealed artifact at all; today an authenticated caller with one valid binding grows three tables per call with no cap (capped only at revision 1<<62 by nextRevision). Owner: W04-01 wording; the growth policy belongs to W04-99 or the artifact owner.

code_findings.finding: putOpaque is a forked copy of store.go put() that keeps the domain_versions append-only bookkeeping but drops three behaviours the accepted path enforces: the Contracts.Entities kind allow-list, the 1<<63-1 revision-overflow precheck, and the receipt_hash immutability refusal. domain_versions append-only semantics themselves ARE preserved - the versions_no_update/versions_no_delete triggers still fire and V18 shows the domain-level CAS is the part with no test. Nothing ever points a VersionRef at these kinds, which is correct: WorkspaceBinding, BootstrapStage and BootstrapReplay are absent from the pinned entity_type enum, and I confirmed against spec/v2.0/contracts/domain.schema.json.
code_findings.recommendation: Judgement: legitimate reuse rather than a second architecture - the kinds are not contract entities, the reference fields are plain strings in the published BootstrapPayload/WorkspaceBinding defs, and the rows are graded against those published defs by the caller. The risk is drift from put(). Fold put() and putOpaque into one writer that takes a grader and keeps the overflow and immutability checks, and add a mutation-visible assertion that a stale revision is refused. Owner: W04-01 rework or the next card touching store.go.

code_findings.finding: Both look up command ids with no principal filter, so a caller who guesses a used command id learns it exists: bootstrap answers 409 COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT before any workspace right is consulted, and register does the same. The ordering is documented in both call sites and I verified it behaves as described (REG-COLLISION-NOT-DISCLOSED-TO-UNAUTHORISED proves register refuses a caller without project rights before naming the collision), but bootstrap has no equivalent ordering - it answers the collision before authorisation, which register deliberately does not.
code_findings.recommendation: The asymmetry is real and under-disclosed: register gates on project-creation rights first, bootstrap does not. Either gate bootstrap the same way, or state in the receipt that bootstrap leaks command-id existence to any authenticated principal. Owner: W04-01 rework.

code_findings.finding: upload() stamps expires_at = now + 1h with the real clock, but every reader of sealed bytes filters only on sealed=1 (acceptance.go:212, changes.go:29, candidates.go:125, backup_recovery.go:43 and nine more), and the only uploaded_content triggers are content_immutable and content_no_delete, which prevent deletion of sealed rows. So a sealed inventory cannot become unreadable after an hour. This is the accepted W02/W03 storage pattern, inherited not introduced - not a W04-01 defect - but the Artifact row carries an expiry that nothing honours.
code_findings.recommendation: Leave the behaviour, and have the storage owner either drop expires_at from sealed rows or document it as pre-seal-only.

code_findings.finding: I verified the emitted reply against the pinned def myself: project_profile_ref is a VersionRef whose entity_type ProjectProfile is in the enum, inventory_artifact_ref is an ArtifactRef, bootstrap_task_id and bootstrap_run_id are plain nullable strings, additionalProperties false. So naming the durable LOCAL_INVENTORY stage record in bootstrap_task_id is contract-legal, not invented. Grading is enforced inside product code, not only in the test. The card's 不虚构完成初始化 rule is satisfied in substance: V12 shows promoting any later stage fails five named assertions, bootstrap_run_id stays nil, and INV-NO-EXTRA-STAGE-INVENTED bounds the stage set.
code_findings.recommendation: No change; the field name is misleading and worth a comment cross-reference where W04-02 creates the real Task.

code_findings.finding: V24 removes the Windows root-escape comparison in escapesRoot and PASS 123 survives, because reparsePoint() short-circuits the || before it. The receipt's disclosed defect 3 credits both layers; only the reparse-attribute probe is exercised by the fixture.

assertion_quality.count_verified: three direct runs and two dispatched runs all report assertions == len(assertion_ids) == 123 with unique ids; the id list equals check_report.json exactly and in order; the source has 130 ok() call sites and 125 distinct labels, the difference being five branch-alternative labels
cannot_fail: INV-LINK-NEVER-BRIDGES-OUTSIDE-CONTENT - dead as written. inventoryBytes()/artifactID() select with `SELECT id FROM domain_objects WHERE project=? AND kind='Artifact' LIMIT 1`, no ORDER BY, so with three artifacts for alpha it returns an arbitrary early row, never the junction-scan row. Proof: injecting the out-of-scope marker string into the current scan's entry Notes (V11b) still gives PASS 123, while the same injection combined with ORDER BY rowid DESC gives FAIL on exactly that id. Fix: order the artifact lookup by revision/rowid DESC (or take the ref from the reply) and assert that no entry location_ref begins with the junction path.

ISOLATION-INVENTORIES-CARRY-OWN-MODULE-ONLY - its positive conjunct `contains(alphaInv,'sha256:')` is already implied by INV-GO-MODULE-FOUND and INV-CONTENT-NONEMPTY, and its negative conjunct repeats the exact string INV-NO-FILE-CONTENT-STORED checks, against a scanner that provably never stores content. It asserts neither inventory's own module ownership, and the name overstates what is measured. Fix: assert that beta's authorized_scope_refs equals beta's ref and that every beta entry location_ref resolves inside beta, and that no beta entry names an alpha-only path.

LIFE-SWAPPED-DIRECTORY-REFUSED - `e != nil && !strings.Contains(errText(e),'NOT_ACCESSIBLE') == false || e != nil` reduces by precedence to `e != nil`: `(e!=nil && contains) || (e!=nil)` == `e != nil`. The `|| e != nil` makes the whole test just 'some error'. It is still caught (V13 fails it) but any unrelated error passes, so it does not verify the card's 'unreadable directory is not treated as empty' claim at bootstrap. Fix: `e != nil && strings.Contains(errText(e), 'NOT_ACCESSIBLE')` - or, if a rename is expected to surface as PATH_OUT_OF_SCOPE, assert that exact code and say so.

NEG-FOREIGN-CLIENT-CHOICE-REFUSED - asserts `e != nil && contains(err,'SELECTION_ALREADY_USED') == false`, i.e. any error that is not one particular string. It never names the expected refusal. It does catch the real defect (V1 fails it) only because a successful register would make e nil, so it is not unfailable, but the expectation is accidental rather than stated. Fix: assert the typed refusal, e.g. contains(err,'FORBIDDEN') or 'UNAUTHENTICATED'.

INV-STAGE-HISTORY-GROWS and INV-STAGE-HISTORY-GROWS-BY-ONE assert `count >= 4` and `>= 2` over a run that performs far more writes; they cannot fail unless the whole flow collapses. Fix: capture the count before a single named operation and assert exactly +1 (INV-STAGE-HISTORY-GROWS-BY-ONE already has the right shape; give it a before-value).
self_fulfilling_or_weak: ISOLATION-EACH-PROJECT-OWNS-ITS-ROWS asserts three counts of the same kind: total kind='Project' == 2, alpha's own row == 1, beta's own row == 1. The third conjunct subsumes the first two and none of them covers the stage, artifact or replay rows the id promises ('ITS ROWS'). It does fail under V5a/V5b/V6 so it is not dead, but it is redundant with CONT-ONE-PROJECT-IDENTITY and ISOLATION-TWO-PROFILES. Fix: assert the per-project BootstrapStage/Artifact/BootstrapReplay ownership counts that the id names, or rename it.

CHAIN-REGISTER-REVISION-ONE is `fmt.Sprint(binding['revision']) == '1'` on the value the domain just built for the reply, not the stored row. The task brief describes it as having several || branches; the shipped code has none, so that description does not match this build. It is weak rather than unfailable: the stored revision is covered indirectly by CHAIN-ONE-BINDING-RECORD plus V8. Fix: read the revision from domain_objects as bindingField() already does for other fields.

CHAIN-BOOTSTRAP-ARTIFACT-SEALED checks the body contains the literal key 'sealed_at' rather than that the artifact is sealed, and reads through the same unordered LIMIT 1 lookup. Fix: assert uploaded_content.sealed = 1 for the artifact's storage_key and use the ref from the reply.

ISOLATION-OUTSIDE-MARKER-NEVER-STORED mixes two stale inventory reads with one real DB-wide check (`uploaded_content WHERE bytes LIKE ...`); only the last conjunct is a strong assertion. V23 confirms the family has teeth, so this is a note.
NEG-READER-PROVISIONED appears only in a branch that is not taken in a passing run, so it is a failure-only label rather than a positive assertion.

W04-01-OUTPUT.evidence: A restricted choice plus workspace.register really does mint an authorized_workspace_ref only after path/junction/scope validation, and I broke each gate to prove it: V1 (authority bypass) fails 6 assertions, V2a (path-shaped ref) 2, V3 (escalation) 1, V4a/V4b (replay) 1 and 5, V11 (junction) 1, V13 (ConfirmPath) 1, V5a/V5b (alias continuation) 4 each, V6 (identity row) 7, V8 (repeat churn) 1. The reference has a producer (RegisterWorkspace) and a lifecycle (list, revoke-to-REVOKED, history kept - V15 fails 3). The gap is the lifecycle's principal boundary: V14, V14b, V21 and V22 all survive, and a live probe confirmed a second OWNER can read, list and bootstrap a foreign reference. Also no real native dialog exists yet (disclosed, and out of scope).

W04-01-NEGATIVE.evidence: Treating an absolute path as an authorized reference fails (V2a, two named ids). Treating an unreadable directory as empty fails at the adapter (V10a) but NOT through the domain: V20 shows a scan returning nothing is accepted, and nothing exercises a scanner that reports empty instead of inaccessible. Treating a repeated import as a duplicate permanent identity fails per principal (V5b, V6) - but my probe built the case the card does not cover: two principals choosing the same canonical directory obtain two Projects and two ProjectProfiles (projects_total 3), and a foreign OWNER bootstrap is accepted against another principal's reference. Partial parse failure and the negatives matrix (same-name, cancelled choice, out-of-scope path, unauthorised older project) are covered by named assertions that I reproduced - except the per-file failure record itself (V10b, V10c survive).
